tags: Lower IOP-rise risk than ketone steroids
quick: 1-2 drops in affected eye 4 times daily
Category C; use only if benefit justifies risk
Caution; systemic steroids appear in milk
summary: Loteprednol etabonate is a topical ophthalmic corticosteroid ('soft' or retrometabolic steroid) used for steroid-responsive inflammatory conditions of the eye and for post-operative ocular inflammation. Its ester structure is rapidly inactivated, giving a lower propensity to raise intraocular pressure than ketone steroids such as prednisolone acetate. The suspension must be shaken vigorously before use; the usual dose is 1-2 drops four times daily.
indications: Steroid-responsive inflammatory conditions of the palpebral/bulbar conjunctiva, cornea and anterior segment (e.g., allergic conjunctivitis, acne rosacea, superficial punctate keratitis, herpes zoster keratitis, iritis, cyclitis, selected infective conjunctivitides)

dosage.d: 1-2 drops in affected eye 4 times daily
dosage.n: In first week may increase up to 1 drop every hour if needed

dosage.d: 1-2 drops in operated eye 4 times daily
dosage.n: Begin 24 h after surgery, continue through first 2 weeks post-op

dosage.d: Reassess if no improvement after 2 days

admin: Do not let the dropper tip touch the eye or any surface (contamination risk)
Apply into the conjunctival sac of the affected eye
Do not wear soft contact lenses during treatment (product contains benzalkonium chloride)
moa: Corticosteroids inhibit the inflammatory response by inducing phospholipase A2 inhibitory proteins (lipocortins), which reduce release of arachidonic acid and thereby suppress prostaglandin and leukotriene synthesis. They inhibit edema, fibrin deposition, capillary dilation and proliferation, leukocyte migration, fibroblast proliferation, and collagen deposition. Loteprednol etabonate is structurally similar to prednisolone but lacks the C-20 ketone and is highly lipid-soluble; it is designed to undergo predictable inactivation, limiting its tendency to raise intraocular pressure.

absolute: Most viral diseases of the cornea/conjunctiva including epithelial herpes simplex keratitis (dendritic), vaccinia, varicella
Known/suspected hypersensitivity to any ingredient or to other corticosteroids
relative: Acute purulent eye conditions (steroids may mask/enhance infection)
monitor: Intraocular pressure if used 10 days or longer

preg: Pregnancy Category C. Embryotoxic and teratogenic in animals at oral doses several-fold the maximum clinical dose. There are no adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women; use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is unknown whether topical ophthalmic administration produces detectable quantities in human milk. Systemic steroids appear in milk and could affect the infant; exercise caution when used in a nursing woman.
renal: Not applicable for topical ophthalmic use.
hepatic: Not applicable for topical ophthalmic use.

minor: Benzalkonium chloride preservative may be absorbed by soft contact lenses
interactions.diagnostics: Prolonged use may elevate intraocular pressure — monitor IOP.

serious: Elevated intraocular pressure (may lead to glaucoma and optic nerve damage)
rare: Delayed wound healing / bleb formation after cataract surgery
emergency: Sudden vision loss or severe eye pain suggesting markedly raised IOP or perforation

monitoring: Intraocular pressure (especially if used 10 days or more)
Visual acuity and lens clarity with prolonged use
Symptom response (re-evaluate if no improvement in 2 days)
counsel: Shake the bottle well before each use
Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface to avoid contamination
Do not wear soft contact lenses while using this medicine
Do not stop early; complete the prescribed course
Report worsening pain, redness, itching, or inflammation to your doctor
Keep regular eye-pressure checks if used long term
pk: Local anti-inflammatory effect over hours to days
Rapidly inactivated to inactive metabolites ('soft' steroid)
pearls: A 'soft' (retrometabolic) ester steroid — designed for a lower IOP-elevation risk (1% vs 6% with prednisolone acetate 1% in trials)
Less effective than prednisolone acetate 1% for acute anterior uveitis — not for cases needing a more potent steroid
Must be shaken vigorously before each use to resuspend the drug
Contraindicated in herpes simplex epithelial (dendritic) keratitis and other viral/fungal/mycobacterial eye infections
Monitor IOP if used 10 days or longer; remove contact lenses (benzalkonium chloride)
missed: Instill the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it. Do not double doses.
overdose: Topical ophthalmic overdose is unlikely to cause acute systemic toxicity. Accidental ingestion: little systemic effect expected given rapid inactivation; provide supportive care. Excessive or prolonged ocular use raises the risk of elevated IOP, cataract, and secondary infection.
